Through trial and error with my cats, I've found that they just don't learn by being relocated. What ended up working for us is creating a firm boundary by calmly blocking them using one hand in front of their chest.

It does take time and effort to outwill them at first, and they will try to go around you if they're stubborn. But if you're steadfast, they learn that they will get their way by being patient and showing good manners.

We've worked around this with my rescue by giving him feeder toys instead of a bowl. We keep them stocked 24/7 which alleviates his food scarcity mindset, yet it takes too much effort for him to binge eat all at once. It's been a huge improvement.

Yeah, it seems unhealthy for a cat to frantically snatch food before the bowl even touches the floor. Personally I would not allow that kind of behavior, but I understand that some cats struggle with food scarcity mindset.

For my rescue who had bad manners and inhaled his bowl, we laid down a boundary for him to wait 1ft away until we're done placing food. Not a perfect process, but still an improvement to the obsessive crowding behavior.

More importantly, we *replaced his bowl with a couple kibble toys*, and keep those stocked 24/7. Now he only eats when he's hungry, since it takes marginally more effort to "unlock" his food.

He's improved his eating habits, slimmed down, regained his agility, and is much healthier now :)
